origin.description: Take the square root of each element, pausing after each one and optionally reporting progress.
origin.usage: slow_sqrt_p(x, delay = getOption("progressr.demo.delay", 0.5), stdout = getOption("progressr.demo.stdout", FALSE), message = getOption("progressr.demo.message", TRUE), sticky = getOption("progressr.demo.sticky", TRUE), progress = getOption("progressr.demo.progress", TRUE))

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. A negative element is NaN and warns NaNs produced, once for that sqrt call.

arguments.name: delay
arguments.text: Seconds to pause, split into five sleeps of 0.2 * delay. The default reads progressr.demo.delay, or 0.5 when that option is unset.

arguments.name: stdout
arguments.text: If TRUE, print O: Element #k. When omitted, progressr.slow_sqrt_p.stdout replaces the demo default.

arguments.name: message
arguments.text: If TRUE, signal M: Calculated value. When omitted, progressr.slow_sqrt_p.message replaces the demo default.

arguments.name: sticky
arguments.text: If TRUE, signal a sticky progression every 10 elements. When omitted, progressr.slow_sqrt_p.sticky replaces the demo default.

arguments.name: progress
arguments.text: If TRUE, create a progressor along x. When omitted, progressr.slow_sqrt_p.progress replaces the demo default.

origin.details: The loop matches slow_sum_p. The progress message is P: Calculating sqrt of the 1-based index. The result is always double.
origin.value: A numeric vector of square roots.
origin.example:
value <- slow_sqrt_p(c(4, 9), delay = 0, message = FALSE, stdout = FALSE, sticky = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("slow_sqrt_p(c(4, 9)) returns %s.\n", paste(format(value, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE), collapse = ", ")))

translation.description: Take the square root of each element, pausing after each one and optionally reporting progress.
translation.usage: slow_sqrt_p(x, delay=<omitted>, stdout=<omitted>, message=<omitted>, sticky=<omitted>, progress=<omitted>)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. A negative element is NaN and warns NaNs produced, once for that call.

arguments.name: delay
arguments.text: Seconds to pause, split into five sleeps of 0.2 * delay. Omitted reads progressr.demo.delay, or 0.5 when that option is unset.

arguments.text: If True, print O: Element #k. Omitted reads progressr.slow_sqrt_p.stdout. An explicit False does not.

arguments.name: sticky

arguments.name: progress
arguments.text: If True, create a progressor along x. Omitted reads progressr.slow_sqrt_p.progress.

translation.details: The loop matches slow_sum_p. The progress message is P: Calculating sqrt of the 1-based index. The result is a list of floats. A negative value warns once and returns NaN.
translation.example:
from progressr.demo import slow_sqrt_p
value = slow_sqrt_p([4, 9], delay=0, message=False, stdout=False, sticky=False, progress=False)
print("slow_sqrt_p(c(4, 9)) returns " + ", ".join(format(item, "g") for item in value) + ".")
